title.en: Ordered pairs, Cartesian product and relations

text.en: A class has 3 boys and 2 girls. The teacher wants to list every possible boy-girl pair for a dance. How many pairs are there, and how do we write them neatly? Mathematics has a tool for exactly this.

keepEnglishTerms: A x B not B x A

text.en:
An ordered pair (a, b) is a pair where the order matters, so (2, 5) is not the same as (5, 2).
For two sets A and B, the Cartesian product A x B is the set of all ordered pairs (a, b) with a in A and b in B.
If A = {1, 2} and B = {x, y, z}, then A x B = {(1,x), (1,y), (1,z), (2,x), (2,y), (2,z)}.
If A has m elements and B has n elements, then A x B has m x n elements, so here 2 x 3 = 6.
In general A x B is not equal to B x A, unless A = B or one of them is empty.
A relation R from A to B is any subset of A x B. We pick the pairs that obey some rule.
The set of first elements of the pairs is the domain, the whole set B is the codomain, and the set of second elements actually used is the range.
A relation from A to B can be shown by an arrow diagram, a table, a graph or as a set of ordered pairs.

problem.en: If A = {1, 2, 3} and B = {2, 4}, write A x B and the relation R = {(a, b): b = 2a}.

why.en: Take each element of A and pair it with each element of B.

text.en: Keep the pairs where b = 2a: (1,2) works because 2 = 2 x 1, and (2,4) works because 4 = 2 x 2.

why.en: Test each pair against the rule.
Domain is the set of first elements, range the set of second elements used.

prompt.en: Explain in your own words what a Cartesian product is and how many pairs A x B has.

requiredIdeas.en: All ordered pairs with first from A and second from B
Number of pairs is m x n
A relation is a subset of A x B

points.en: An ordered pair cares about the order of its two entries.
A x B has n(A) x n(B) elements.
A relation is a subset of A x B; domain = first elements, range = second elements used.
A x B and B x A are usually different.
